name: comp-131

frames.best_why: The dropdown is fully open with all three strategies, their descriptions and a tick on the active one.

tagline: Split button on a pull request row that opens a merge-method menu.
summary: A commit row pairs a title and meta line with a light split button. The wide half shows the chosen merge method; the chevron half drops a menu of three strategies, each explained in a sentence.
appearance: A dark rounded card row holds a bold commit title and a grey meta line on the left. On the right sits a light split control: a wide label segment and a narrow chevron segment. Opening it reveals a grey dropdown where each of three options has a name, a small description and a tick on the active one.
behaviour: Clicking the chevron opens the menu below the button; choosing one of the three radio options moves the tick, closes the menu and swaps the main button's label. The card behind does not move.
demo_content: PR title "feat: add usage-based billing", meta "#482 · 6 commits · checks passed", and three strategy options.
search_phrases: code hosting style merge options menu
button with dropdown arrow for choices
use_when: A primary action has two or three variants a small menu should offer, like choosing how to merge a branch.
avoid_when: The menu descriptions are fixed prose and the main button runs no merge action of its own.
customise: The three strategies come from an options array holding a label and a description; the selected label and menu width are set in the file.
weight_why: A split button and a small radio menu; nothing runs at rest.

a11y.note: The chevron is labelled Options and the menu behaves as a radio group, but the main button performs no action itself.

issues: The main Merge pull request button has no handler, so only the dropdown changes anything.
polish_why: Realistic pull request row and a well described menu; the main action is inert.
title: Merge Strategy Split Button
